rationale: Both solutions do a graph search with correct hex adjacency and have good doc comments. A is more robust. It strips spaces from each line, so it handles boards given in the indented display format from the task. Its start and goal closures cleanly express the difference between the two players without boolean-flag branching. B converts lines to runes directly with no stripping, yet its doc comment says leading spaces are stripped, so the comment misrepresents the code and indented input would break it. B's separate neighbors helper reads well, but it allocates a slice per cell and copies the start slice into the queue redundantly. A's compact neighbour table and DFS are equally clear and more efficient. A wins on robustness and accuracy.
